The decor of the restaurant was very nice and elegant. Once we were sat, we had 1 gentleman come to give us the menus and water. Then another gentleman came to take our wine order. A 3rd gentleman came to open the wine, and a 4th gentleman came to take our food order. I'm not sure if this is how the serving staff works, but it can be confusing. Our french onion soup was very good-rich, cheesy, extremely flavorful. The calamari with lemon/basil dip was phenomenal. We then ordered the 12oz filet for my boyfriend and I to share with the gold mashed potatoes and asparagus. The steak was almost well done (we ordered it medium) and had absolutely no flavor. The sides were very satisfactory though, very tasteful.

The service was great staff was very attentive. A quiet and romantic place to have dinner. Most of the dishes were excellent although I wasn't prepared for the jalapeños that my short ribs came covered in and wasn't listed as part of the entree. The highlights of the meal were the pineapple mojoto, the corn ravioli and the creme brûlée. The side dishes of potato gratin and Yukon mashed potatoes were also fantastic. The waiter was a little cheesy with his comments mostly because I heard him repeating his funny one liners to other tables. I find the steakhouse to a bit overpriced but all in all it was good food. There are other places with much better views but it still felt open and interesting.

I'd go back in a heart beat. Food was excellent. I ate every scrap of my steak and scraped the Bearnaise sauce from the bowl. But the star was the cucumber mint gin martini. It rounded out the whole meal.

Let's start with the decor - very clean, masculine lines. Not over the top elegant, but classy. The service was outstanding - it was our anniversary, which I mentioned on the reservation, and we were congratulated by everyone; nice touch! Waitstaff were knowledgeable and eager to help - not something I find in most Phoenix/Scottsdale restaurants. Now to the food - it was very good, but it didn't knock me over. Excellent quality, portions were adequate, but the menu selections did not WOW me. Also, I wish the food was out of this world for the price I paid - very expensive. In my opinion, J & G Steakhouse is a type of restaurant that I will try once, just to experience what it is, but it is not going to be a destination spot for us.
Wonderful dinner, definitely going again
This is the best opportunity in town. The Neighborhood menu is a major deal with excellent choices and an excellent price for the three course meal.
My husband and I went for our anniversary and had an outstanding experience. The food, service, and atmosphere was amazing!!!! We would HIGHLY recommend J & G to anyone! We will definitely be back!
a fabulous experience at a perfect location
Better service at Denny's! Absolutely the worst service at an expensive restaurant I've experienced in many years.

He were well taken care of-the service was top notch--informative but not obtrusive. The Chef's Tasting Menu was phenomenal. We had a great time discovering different tastes and textures. We look forward to returning to discover the other dishes available.

Fabulous setting. Fabulous cusine. Service is ALWAYS slow. Often we get offered drinks by more than one server and it simply doesn't come. Often the server doesn't come to the table at all for long periods. Once the cusine comes it is delightful but for the level of restaurant that it is too consistently slow ... Other equivalent restaurants in the area (T Cooks, Elements Tarbell's) have superlative service that J&G cannot come close to. Once they manage the service end of the dining experience this restaurant will be a fabulous destination in Phoenix. So if you are patient go enjoy this excellent restaurant !!! But if you are really hungry and need to eat something ... bring some crackers in your purse !!! But I will keep going. I love it.

The restaurant was friendly, clean, and cool in temperature. The view was amazing. Jessie did a great job and worked very hard. He paid extra attention to my special requests. He was aware of the celebratory reason we were there, and he was respectful of our private time. The food was good in temperature, but the presentation was a little sparse. We did have to send the lamb chops back to be cooked more. The sides were the best! We will definitely be back! Thank you

Coming from Chicago, my standards for a good steak are set pretty high. I found that the meat was good, but the seasoning left me wanting. I feel horrible when I have to put salt and pepper onto my steak after it is cooked. It was very nice that they supply a medley of sauces.

The service is some of the best I've had, ever! The staff was very friendly, left us alone at the right times, came to serve us at the right times, had a friendly conversation at the right times. I felt very comfortable throughout the entire meal.

The view was fantastic. I looked up the sunset time before my reservation and made my reservation 15 minutes beforehand...It turned out perfect, once we were settled in our booth, we had a beautiful view.

The dining experience at J&G Steakhouse was outstanding from the moment we were greeted. OUr waiter introduced himself, asked if we had questions, recommended signature cocktails, explained the menu, the specials,and its signature menu items. The service, food and the atmophere was outstanding. THis restaurant definetely exceeded my expectations.

J&G is great for a special occasion due to the lush yet not stiff resort ambiance. Stroll through the lobby and shops first. Make a night of it. Have coctails on the lobby terrace and view the vistas or enjoy the live music at the bar either before or after. J&G  shares the same forever stretching view. Menu is limited but offers something for everyone. Portions are right sized.

Food and service are both excellent. As locals in Phoenix, we love the summer Neighborhood Menu, although limited, it is still one of the best in the Valley. The view is spectacular - especially at sunset. This is not your typical "hotel" restaurant. Highly recommend.
I visited J&G Steakhouse in celebration of my boyfriend's 30th Birthday. I couldn't have asked for anything better. I will be more than happy to recommend this to any one and everyone!
Food was good, buy my steak wasn't cooked properly and had to be sent back to the kitchen. My martini also was not chilled well - plus, I don't really want a martini in a champagne glass.
Fantastic everything. Solid menu with choices for everyone. But if you choose the steak, it is out of this world! Definitely recommended.
Just Great !!! we will be back.
Service, ambiance, food.....superb!

Good food, great views, Romantic atmosphere overshadowed by noise.
Great steak restaurant overall.

On prior visits, this was one of our favorite restaurants. Not on May 14th-my birthday-server was erratic and service from the kitchen was unacceptable. Two dishes were returned and had not been replaced in twenty minutes-we ultimately cancelled them so two out of four of our party had no entrees. The restaurant was moderately busy so this was really inexcusable.

Steak was excellent. The preparation of the halibut needed help. It appeared to have been steamed and would have been better grilled or broiled. We would not order that again! Service was excellent and the view is the best that Scottsdale has to offer.
Everything was fantastic. The food, the service, the view.....it was a perfect night.

We have been there twice, and the food does not meet my expectations for a chef of Vongerichten's reputation. The dishes rely too heavily on cream and butter for flavor. However, the restaurant itself is very beautiful and has a nice view. Dinner was lovely for that reason.
We enjoyed our evening dining on the terrace with a great view of the Phoenix area. Good food and great service. We will dine there again.
The Food and Beautiful view was great...my wife and I really enjoyed our dinner experience at J&G Steakhouse. We would definitely come back and recommend the restaurant to our friends and family.
What a shame that Mary Elaine's has turned into such a dark, stark, expensive delicious food with poor service and lots of noise.
The dinner was outstanding. A very nice view of the city lights. very romantic.

J&G is a great steakhouse. If you go there looking for pasta and aren't happy, get over it, 'cause it's a steakhouse. Best I can say for it is that my dad, who is never, ever happy with his food said his steak was "perfect". So if you're in the mood for a perfect steak with great service and a fabulous view of Phoenix, go. Keep in mind that premium service and food do come at a price, so you will have to pay for it, but if you have a special occasion and like steak, go for it. The asparagus sides I had were absolutely outstanding. Not a tough or stringy square inch among them. And the deserts (try the warm chocolate cake--mine was poached by my entire table) are excellent as well. The only gripe is a bit too much noise.
Highly recommend the chef's tasting menu!

The Side Dishes of Mushrooms and Tuna Tare Tare was very good. I ordered the salmon but instead of the mashed potatoes, I ordered the sauteed spinach. What was interesting about the spinach was that it had a hint of mint in the spinach which was quite good. It does however need a bit of salt, so if you like bland, then the sauteed spinach is for you. The view was miraculous and they had an outdoor are to sit which most people seemed to be smoking cigars, but definitely ROMANTIC place to go. I plan to go back and possibly stay at the resort. Very nice area but only seen it at night.
Awesome Restaurant on 5th Floor of Phoenician Hotel with a fantastic view of the city. You can eat inside or out on the terrace. We where in town for 5 days - best food we had on our trip!
Meal was excellent, however avoid the very disappointing Cesare Salad which was chopped romaine hearts with little dressing.

Asked for tablet with nice view. Table for two was by the window but my back was to the window (no view). Wife had the lobster and she enjoyed it very much. I ordered a filet, ordered it med rare, was cooked more medium - it was good but not the best I've ever had. Patio very nice. Dessert touch also very nice.

I was very disappointed in this restaurant. The food was overpriced for the quality. The restaurant was so dark that My husband had a hard time reading his menu. We have eaten at a lot of his restaurants and were excited to try this one. How disappointing! There are much better restaurants in Scottsdale to spend your hard earned money at.

Very nice serving staff. Parmesian encrusted chicken with Avacado was incredible. Apsarigus and hand cut fries. My daughter had 8 oz filet. The made-from-scratch real ginger ail and a cherry blossom soda from the bar were very tasty and unique drinks. The Chocolate cake was fantastic. Nice atmosphere for a formal or special occasion. drive right up to the front door, use the free valet parking service, and walk though the lobby of the Phonecian resort to add some class to the meal. Overall an enjoyable experience.

One word... Phenomeal! J&G's is romantic, and moreover delicious. The atmosphere was gorgeous, with two roaring fires on the patio. The service and food both exceeded our expectations. Traveling quite often and hitting some of the best spots nationwide, this one ranks right at the top! If you are looking for a great steak, mouthwatering desert and terrific service, this is your place! We LOVED J&G's! One last note- Because the restaurant seated us 25 minutes later than our reserved time, they comped our ENTIRE bar bill. Like I said, exceptional service!

We went for Valentine's Dinner. We were seated promptly with a lovely view of the southeaset Valley. The service was less than what was to be expected. There was a mix-up on the course order and the drink service was slow. However, the food was excellent. The value of the meal was also good.
Totally delicious. The fois gras was sensational and the steak tasty.

My wife and I went their for a Valentine's dinner. The views overlooking the valley are amazing. I thought the prices were on par with the other high-end steak houses although I don't think their filet was quiet up to Mastro's. My wife had a salmon dish that she raved about. The Oysters were very nice, and my wife liked the ahi. The wine list is good but not great. Service was good but again not as good as Mastros. We had to flag her down a few times which is unacceptable at a high-end restaurant. In the end, I would recommend if you want pretty good food with fantastic scenery.

My husband and I really enjoyed our Valentine celebration dining experience. We both ordered the filet mignon and found our steaks perfectly cooked - high quality steaks. We also enjoyed our sides, the salt and pepper baked potato and asparagus (each side was large enough for us two to share). We also shared a piece of the carrot cake - we both agreed the carrot cake was the best we had ever had - so moist and the cream cheese frosting was amazing. The carrot sorbet and cream cheese ice cream scoops on the side were superb flavor combinations. And, of course, the view of the city lights and Papago Peaks were phenomenal - we were seated by the window - though there is hardly a bad seat to be found. We will return!

Our dinner was fantastic! I had the filet and my husband hed the pepper crusted ribeye. They bring you a sampler of three different sauces to try with your steaks that were all great. The risotto with mushrooms was wonderful and the scalloped potato and roasted mushroom sides were delicious. The restaurant was beautiful with a great view and they were able to accomodate the request I made for a window table when I made my reservation.

One of the best things was that this was our anniversary which I indicated when I made the reservation. The server and the manager both wished us happy anniversary and when our dessert of cheesecake (yum!) arrived they had personalized around the edge of the plate Happy 15th Anniversary! A nice touch!
There are several good restaurants in Phoenix and a few great ones. J&G Steakhouse is in a class by itself at the top. Everything, from the food to the service, was excellent.
They gave us a tablet down fron and we had a view of the total Phoenix valley! Best View in Scottsdale! Food was excellant!
Very nice experience...only complaint...had a hard time getting a second cup of coffee after dessert...will definitely go back...and would recommend this rest. to others....

My husband and I went had dinner at J&G over the weekend. The restaurant is beautiful and very classy. The service and the food outstanding. We were treated like royalty and cant wait to go again. Didnt want to leave! It was my birthday and they provided a complimentary dessert and coffee, very unexpected. Beautiful experience would recommend to all for an awesome time.

Our waitress asked every question using "We". "Are we ready to make some decisions? Do we have any questions? How are things tasting for us?" It was VERY annoying. She was not eating with us! The dinner was OK. Would not return.
The tasting menu was an amazing value. It was a memorable dining experience.
Expected more from a Jean George restaurant. Food excellent, preparation request missed, service slow and awkward.

The restaurant has a great view of Scottsdale/Phoenix. The terrace has firepits to keep warm and enjoy the view. The ambiance is very simplistic yet chic. A place to go to be seen. Very good for a romantic evening or special occasion.

We had a wonderful Christmas Eve dinner with our two adult children. We thoroughly enjoyed everything and everyone there. The food was fantastic and we felt right at home for being away for the holiday. Thank you.
Tara & Gary Slowik (Lauren & Chris Slowik-Children)

This is a very beautiful restaurant. The steak was excellent. I had the Caesar salad, New York strip, the mashed potatoes, and the chocolate cake with the caramel icecream. I also had a taste of the Blue Point oysters, tuna tartare, potato gratin, and french fries.
The Caesar had a mayonnaise quality to it than and I would have like more of the classic Anchovy/Worcestershire flavor. The mashed was a bit on the heavy side although the taste was fine. The steak was cooked perfectly and probably one of the best steaks I have had here in Phoenix. When I return I will order the 24 oz. Porterhouse and leave out the Caesar and mashed potatoes. The tartare and oysters were beautiful.
Great Dinner food terrific service perfect view overlooking the city.

Great setting and decor, overlooking the impressive, opulent swimming pools at the Phoenecian. Excellent food, great wine list and helpful staff. Our only complaint was a large nearby table featuring 4 small, largely unsupervised children, whose t-shirted/blue jeaned/flip flopped parents were content to ignore the running, giggling and messes. It detracted from what could have been a spectacular evening.

Overall, the experience was what we expected for a brand name restaurant in an upscale resort. A few comments on the food for those thinking of eating here. The sides are about 1 1/2 servings worth of food. For the two of us, two sides were about right. The filet that my wife ordered was cooked perfectly and was a very nice piece of meat. I ordered (and paid for) the 18 oz Prime Rib Eye, medium rare. I've got a preconceived notion of what an 18 oz Prime Rib Eye cooked to medium rare should be. I'm pretty sure that what I received was a veal chop. A 12-14 oz bone in veal chop. A veal chop that was thin enough that cooking it to medium rare would have been pretty near impossible with a broiling technique. It tasted good though.

I really like the revamped dining room at Phoenician to a Jean George Steakhouse. Food was excellent and well presented but service and detail started off well and faltered several times. Great view worth a visit....

The food and atmosphere were great. I requested and was seated at an execellent table with a scenic view of the valley.The service was a tad slow, and when I made the reservation through your site I requested a piece of cake for my wife's birthday after our meal. This was not supplied, and we just had a small deccert from thier menu. Definetly a return visit in the future.
Very upscale but relaxed feel to the place - Great service excellent ambiance- Pricy but worth it
We had a lovely aniversary dinner. Beautiful decor and great service.
Everything was outstanding - food, service, ambiance,   we will definitely return.

This was an overpriced resort restaurant. This is not affiliated with the Phoenician Resort, I found out that they only lease the space to this establishment. The food was terrible, the french onion soup was too salty & thick, the calamari had too much very bland breading as a coating & all of our steaks were dried out (I had a filet & was so disappointed, this cut of meat should have melted in my mouth !!) As for our kids chicken, it didn't note that it was both white & dark meat (most chicken dishes are white meat, a healthier choice). The drinks were so overpriced, and when the waiter spilled my daughter in-laws drink, he only brought back 1/2 glass, poor call on the waiters decision. Not enough room to note all the bad, just don't go

Outside would have been more romantic and quiet. Food was excellent. More casual than we thought it would be. Families, bar and TV nearby, moderately loud. Would go again but with different expectations.

Nice location. Not great service. Food was not great. sorry to say. Lighting outside needs work. I could not see my food. Waiter was a little off. lose the french fries in favor for some real ones. Salad was ok Bread was good. you need a bone in filet imho

Regards.
Very good steak house, nothing dry aged but all prime, with very reasonable prices. Dessert was great as was the service and the drinks. Would definitely return.
EVERYTHING WAS THE FINEST WE HAD EVER EXPERIENCED!!!!!

They seem to be struggling...but why? Wonderful food, great view, attentive service and reasonable prices (for the high level of product they use). I'll always think of the beautiful modern space they've created as Mary Elaine's at The Phoenician but you should get over it...even if it's just for their burger and a beer special in the lounge for $19. and watch for more specials if they continue having troubles filling the place. A beautiful sunset is never better than on the Terrace of J & G Steakhouse.
My 4 other guests had not been to the restaurant before and we all had a fine dinner and great service. My compliments to the Chef.

Food was fantastic -- no complaints. However, it took well over an hour to receive our entrees. Not the waiter's fault, obviously. We noticed that several people were upset about how long it was taking to receive their food.

Wine list was decent -- some very good selections at the typical 100% mark-up. The wait staff was very good.
How do you top perfection? I must admit the dover sole is the best I have ever eaten and prepared beautifuly.
We had such a wonderful experience. The view is perfect; the waitress was friendly and kind. The food and service was fantastic! It's our new favorite place.
Great dining experience. Highly recommended.
The food was good but not memorable....Mastros is better for steak. The views and beauty of the restaurant makes up for what it lacks in food quality.

My husband and I enjoyed our dinner there, celebrating our first anniversary. The staff was very attentive. I think there were 8 different people servicing our table (which was a little overwhelming by the end because we didn't know who we should ask for what), but we never waited too long for attention. The food was delicious and straight forward. The cocktails, however, were complex and new and so amazing! I had the Amelia and my husband had the Dark and Stormy. Yum. For our dessert they brought out molten chocolate cake and on the plate they had very deftly written "Happy 1st Anniversary" which was adorable. We had a lovely time and the view was truly special.

We LOVED our dinner at J&G. Impeccable but friendly service. Outstanding food. The best apple tart I have ever eaten. Plus, the dining room was lively but not a "scene", tastefully done, and had outstanding views.

This was a nice change from Mary Elaine's if you prefer a more traditional American menu with especially well prepared steaks. The setting is beautiful at the Phoenecian and the lighting and color scheme is subdued and romantic. My wife had halibut and I had a filet and both were done perfectly. Everything is ala carte which was no surprise. Prices were comparable with other higher end steak houses in the Valley. I would definitely recommend this over Bourbon Steak at the Fairmont-better dining experience and better value. One oddity to mention at the bar. The bartenders use a glass "shaker" to stir martinis/manhattans and the drinks don't get cold. However, they use a metal shaker for other cocktails. Had to put an ice cube in my martini.
We had a wonderful experience at J&G Steakhouse....it was our first visit and we will definitely be back...the food was excellent and the whole atmosphere was great. Great views.

Overall our experience was very good, but nothing was outstanding. The food was well prepared and did not disappoint. However we were not "wowed" either. The service was excellent with the exception of the hostess staff which was a bit short with us when we asked to move our reservation. The view/ambiance is the star of this restaurant.
Nice view but the side by side seating is uncomfortable for a couple.
Incredible views, great service, excellent food and wonderful ambiance

Special promotional menu for Scottsdale Restaurant Week - main course of steak was tough and nearly inedible. Service was very slow. Poor decision by the restaurant to skimp on the promotional food...now we are unlikely to ever come back.

We participated in the "restaurant week" dinner so we were limited choice of three apps, entrees, desserts. However, we ordered a separate appetizer to start, the deep fried calamari that came out literally dripping in grease. When you placed one of the rings on your plate it left a circle of grease, when pressed with a fork, it literally gushed. The lemon aioli was so over lemony it made your lips pucker. service was moderate although they did manage to get the order mixed up and fired well before we were ready for the entree. Wines were a a 4 oz pour at about 2/3 the retail price of a whole bottle (26.5 oz- you do the math). Overall it was a disappointing meal for us, especially remembering Marie Elaine's. Mediocre steakhouse.
Starting with the view & city lights to the ambiance, service and excellent food, it was a great choice.

Based on our experience this was quite over rated and a real disappointment for this foursome. The Cesar and Chicken were what one would expect from a fast food chain restaurant. There was absolutely no sauce on the chicken and it was very salty. The Cesar Salad was poor quality lettuce, overdressed, and unpleasant. The Apple Tartine was far from anything memorable. The concept of Restaurant Week, I presume, which is a fabulous idea by the way, allows local residents to sample various venues and encourage repeat dining. This was a poor and lazy effort on the part of J&G, a purported well rated dining establishment. We obviously will not be returning.

I had high expectations of this restaurant as it replaced the renowned Mary Elaine's.
As to be expected, the service and view were excellent. I was not too thrilled with the quality of food but maybe because I ordered the restaurant week menu. The best part of the meal was the steamed shrimp salad. The steak and frites was average and the dessert was comforting but not spectacular. It's worth trying it out.

We live two minutes from the Phoenician and would not have gone to J & G on an average Saturday night had it not been for Restaurant Week. We loved it and will go back - can't wait to take out of town guests. The service was great and it's a beautiful restaurant without being too stuffy. We also enjoyed walking out on the balcony with our wine after dinner.
We had the greatest time.. the food the best Troy the server excellent

This restaurant seems to be pretty much what is promised. Decent food and steaks. It follows the awful trend in the valley to put a steak house in every hotel. The food we had was fine except for the yukon gold potatoes had the consistency of paste. Our captain and his assistant did a very fine job. When we arrived we stood for several minutes in front of the reception desk totally ingnored while three girls fusted about the reservations and talked with one another. The remodel is mostly a waste of money as parts are impressive and others not. The noise level is unbelieveable!!! If you want a enjoyable evening this is not it. If you want to party and rock than go for it! Very Disappointing for a Five Star Hotel & Jean George!!!

The ambiance was great but the food was less than I expected. Although the restaurant did not seem that busy, our server seemed as though he didn't have time for us but was doing all he could. Overall, it was good but less than I expected as a foodie!

The Food, Ambiance and Service was terrific. One of the best the Valley offers. But lets discuss the BAR....a martini, served in a wine glass! Warm! and I asked for the high end vodka which was pulled from the area in bar which has a window with sun coming into it. Warm vodka such a mistake! The waitress did bring me some ice to add to my drink but those were HUGE cubes of ice not even shaved or crushed...the specialty drinks were either way to sour that the ice had to melt to make it drinkable or so dull that we finally had to send it back it was drinkable for any of the group. When I go out to eat I want food and drinks. Please consider getting the Bar Area to go through a overhaul.
The view is fabulous! The service is deliberately slow so dinner took us almost 2 hours.

Regarding the food, half of the courses served were outstanding.
Shrimp Salad was among the best we've every enjoyed.
Deserts were all outstanding.

On the other hand,
The salmon, while extremely tender, was too bland.
The steak also needed more seasoning.
The Caesar Salad tasted of vinegar, not anchovies.
the view is magnificant, waite staff very accomodating even to the most persnikity in our group, looking forward to a return visit
Wonderful view, food and service..a lovely restaurant and a very memorable meal..we will be back!

Since inhabiting the former Mary Elaine spot J&G has remodeled to great effect. The dining room is filed with warm colors, wood accents, richly colored leather and carpets. Some tables overlook popago and the valley. The butcher block tables, craft place mats, & switchblade styled steak knives add to the no pretense steakhouse feel. The wine selection to offers bottles below $100 to $1,000+. The chateau neuf de pope wasn't the best we've had so perhaps they need to hire a sommelier. Great service from all staff. Outstanding sides and steaks on par with other similarly priced steakhouses. If the steaks were extraordinary J&G would get the ultimate recommendation. Go for the ambience and good food, for the BEST steak look elsewhere.

The service was considerably less than the food and ambiance. For example, we got served our salads before our appetizer? I've never seen that happen. All in all, this was a great place I am sure we'll return to.

Very good; could be better. My wife has had better tuna tartare elsewhere, and there was too much vinegar in the bearnaise sauce for her steak. My pork belly appetizer was very good and my short rib excellent. My mother really liked her beet salad; her crab cake was OK. Service very attentive, and timing excellent.
Decent food in very nice setting. Wine prices on bottles reflect very big mark-up.

The dining environment was superb with a great view but most importantly, the steak was phenomenal! Accompanying that great bone-in rib eye were the best au gratin potatoes I've ever had. The service was impeccable and not intrusive. Morton's had been my standard to judge others by. This is now the one. I will return on my next visit.

A pale shadow of the Prime operation that Jean-Georges runs in Las Vegas. The room is far too dark, possibly to maximize views out the picture windows. The service was confused and amateurish. The food was acceptable for the most part, but had notable lapses including a $60 porterhouse that had no flavor at all. The wine list is fair with higher than usual markups on mostly familiar wines.
A great place to dine for a special occasion. The view is outstanding and the food is superb. You will not be let down!

The steaks were only fair at best for a high dollar steakhouse. The wait staff had to be asked numerous times to just refill the water glasses. The side dishes were bland. Maybe Friday night is not their best night for dining.
Food was good, service was fair, asked for extra items like more butter and salt and pepper and felt like they were doing us a favor.

My wife and I went to J&G to celebrate our anniversary. Not only was she impressed as we made our way up to the restaurant, but the experience was top notch all around. The food was superb and reasonably priced. The service was excellent and what a view! I'll definitely visit here again, once I can save a few extra dollars.

Our first time in Scottsdale from Washington D.C. We had just gotten off an 8 hour flight (with delays/layovers) and were looking to wind down. This was the perfect place at the Phoenician. I cannot overstate how attentive the staff were. The food was absolutely delicious considering we were jet lagged and usually have decreased apetite.
Highly recommend for a romantic evening. Beautiful view of the Valley

I dined here with my husband for our 4th anniversary. We were seated at the window with a phenominal view. The restaurant was more urban and chic in feel than your tradiditonal steakhouse. Service was great and the food more than lived up to being one of Jean George's restaurants. There is a lot of steakhouse competetiton in the valley now, but this wins hands down. Sorry Randy!

Thre were 4 things that went wrong with our experience; (1)Halibut was overcooked (2)Th replacement wasn't that much better (3)They charged us twice for the halibut!!!!!! We hd to remind them o take one off (4) My wine by the glass wasn't filled completely and waitress said she would open a new bottle to fill the glass but forgot.

A very pleasant dining experience. A variety of interesting appetizers is available. The beet salad was delicate and very tasty, but the Caesar salad lacked pizzazz and was just adequate with unexciting dressing and too crunchy croutons. If you run a “steak house” you better be able to produce a memorable piece of beef. And J&G’s certainly can do that! Steaks were cooked absolutely perfectly to order. The 8 ounce filet seemed more like 10 ounces, making it a bargain, and it was succulent and delicious. Presentation was beautiful and high caliber.

I would rate J&G Steak house as a hidden bargain vs. the overpriced “high-end” steak house chains in the Valley. Great beef, reasonable prices, and exemplary staff and décor combined perfectly.

While the food was very good, it was much more expensive than the other excellent Phoenix steak houses, with smaller sides, and no extra special service to make it worth the difference in price. It was a birthday celebration, noted on the Open Table notes, and nothing special was really added for the event. With so many steak houses to choose from, its unlikely that we'll return.
Excellent food and service, thought the prices were very reasonable for the quality would highly reccomend. After dinner we finished our wine on the patio/deck outstanding views.
This is a beautiful restaurant, great place to have dinner. The staff is very attentive but not overbearing. I will go back.
The service was excellent but the food wasn't worth the price.
VERY EXPENSIVE....poor service from our primary waiter, but the support staff was FABULOUS... too many other GREAT steak houses in town to return to this mediocre one.
Excellent food and very reasonable for a prime steakhouse. Nice view. Top notch service. I will be back.

Excellent -- definitely the best steak place in Phoenix/Scottsdale. Love that you get to try as many sauces as you want for no fee (vs. BLT Steak where you only get one sauce and have to pay for each additional sauce separately or Mastro's where there aren't any sauces at all). Filet mignon was incredible, and sides are delicious and more interesting than most other steak places. Amazing view, and service was great. Impressive wine list. Not stuffy or formal, and value for the price was excellent. Loved everything that we ordered. Would definitely go back!

Excellent steak restaurant. Hangar steak was flavorful and cooked to a perfect medium request. Very reasonable price for the hangar. Bar is also great and can get a good hamburger but why pass on the 20 dollar hangar. Great views of the valley.

Very informative server and overall level of service. Good variety of choices and interesting selections. Only downside was an undercooked lobster dish that should not have left the kitchen. Great ambiance and views.

Amazing experience. Very nice decor and absolutely impeccable service. Huckleberry bellini was wonderful. Beet salad was nice, but forgettable as well as the glass of local AZ wine presented with dinner. The lamb was wonderful, especially with the black peppercorn sauce. I do have to say that the waiter attempted to offer me other glasses of wine, but I chose not to trouble the establishment with waiting on me hand and foot :o) The butter cookie with coconut cream and raspberries was a nice, light end to a beautiful meal with a beautiful view. I was treated very respectfully and kindly by all staff. I would recommend this to anyone going near Phoenix or Scottsdale.
One word...excellent! Service was fantastic, food was delicious. Thank you for the wonderful experience at The Phoenician. Our waiter was quite personable and a pleasure.

Loved it. Best Halibut I've had in a while. The staff went out of their way to be friendly and make us feel like regulars. Beautifully decorated, amazing view of the city lights and you can't beat the beauty of the resort. Kudos to the manager Michael Shapiro who was on hand and jumped in when his wait staff was busy. He was great! But the real star (no offense Michael)....is the food!
Great restaurant, great food great service.
Very overpriced for what it was. Pretended to be high end, luxury steakhouse dining and turned out to be just overpriced ordinary fare. Very disapponited!
The food was a 10. The bar service was great. The table service mediocre. The decor in the restaurant is very disturbing and uncomfortable.

j&g is very promising. the food was pretty good its just going through some growing pains and service on a mondy night left a LOT to be desired. there seems to be a wide range of experience in the staff making it hit or miss. great drinks and great views. i will try again in 6 months.
The views were amazing. I loved the decor and the bar area. I would go back for drinks and appetizers. The food was ok...nothing outstanding. I much prefer the other steakhouses in the area.

One of the better steaks I have had and I have had some good steaks in the better restaurants. Very cool decor, much different than its predecessor. Big problem with noise level. The two of us found ourselves shouting as the tables with more than 2 were so loud in order for those dining to be heard. Would not go with more than 1 person for this reason. While manager suggested a good wine, the list of embarrasing for a restaurant of this caliber. The total list equaled the number of reds found in most fine steak houses. Good oysters, fair tuna tartare and excellent carrot cake.
small portions, detached server, food good, nothing special
Definately a major "come down" from the previous Mary Elaine's at this location. Didn't expect it to be Mary Elaine's, but this was nothing special at all.

Gorgeous, brand new space with the same wonderful view. Service was highly trained and smooth but our server fell behind as the restaurant reached its peak capacity. When my wife's filet was overcooked it was addressed graciously, she was given a free appetizer to eat while a new steak was cooked properly. Our second bottle of water was quite delayed but we were not charged for it. The lamb chops I had were super. You get to have up to 7 sauces with your meat, which was a unique touch. Overall, I put this in my top 5 or so, but they're going to have to do better to be one of my 3 favorites
Beautiful  view of the city from the balcony. the lighting was actually quite good and the food was tasteworthy. Will go back again

J&G surpassed my expectations.Having dined before at this venue when it was Mary Elaines,I was impressed by the transition. The Pork Belly and Steak Tartare appetizers were both outstanding and generous. Both our cuts of Beef were expertly prepared. When you combine the view, food quality, and service, it is difficult to understand how reasonably priced this restaurant is. What a pleasant surprise!!

Quite a shockingly big difference from Mary Elaine - and I am not saying it in a felicitous way. I ordered their, most expensive,largest prime rib eye. It's not prime rib but a rib eye. I could have bought a one-inch thick 28 oz. prime rib from Fry's and cooked it better with rosemary, olive oil, etc. - and at the doneness I wanted it to be. I wanted medium rare - on the rare side. It came medium on the medium-well side. So disappointing. Their French fries is not pomme frites - and I thought the resident chef was a French. The fries are sliced thick, just like McDonald's and cooked soft like McDonalds And gone is the thick list of a wine list. Gone are the verticals of various bordeaux, burgundy. California and Australia reds.

Great execution of the menu items. Wonderful resort setting with a view overlooking the city. But, it is another steakhouse; seems like we have too many of these popping up in Phoenix. Expensive: $55 for Dover sole?
Our experience was absolutely wonderful; ambience, food ,service were a great.

NY Steak was one of the best steaks I've ever had. Cheesecake with Sour Cherry Sorbet is incredible. This restaurant far exceeded expectations. Great view and excellent atmosphere. Make time for a pre or post dinner cocktail on the balcony.

We enjoyed nearly every bite of every dish we ordered. peppercorn N.Y. Strip and steak tartare were quite good although the frites that came with the tartare were neither hot nor crispy. The meat sauces are delightful and the bearnaise seems whipped it's so light but just as flavorful as a heavier sauce would be. The pork belly and short rib were the standout hits for us. Both cooked to mouth watering perfection and an incredible value as well. The creamed spinach was overpowered by waaay toooo much garlic for this garlic lover...losing the spinach entirely! Not good, but we ate it anyway and the Parker House rolls are nice but not fresh out of the oven. The service needs some tweaking. Our waiter was good but was overwhelmed.

My husband and I enjoyed our visit to J&G very much. The food was outstanding and the service was very attentive without being pretentious. The beer list was also quite good as was the wine list that had several price points. J&G is more casual than MaryElaine's which used to occupy the space. My husband thought the decor was very early 1970's. I likened it to the set of the old t.v. show "Playboy After Dark." During the first hour we were at the restaurant the music was abit of a distraction. But by the second hour it was more soothing.
Food was good. Servers looked lost
excellent experience after the table with the small screaming child left

it's was my birthday, from the moment we arrived till we left, the evening was perfect
we told all our friends
we will be back
thank you
larry perlstein
Had a wonderful meal. The sweetcorn ravioli(appetizer) was out of this world. There were 6 in our group and everyone had a wonderful meal. Will go back next time in town.
